name: Qt-Secret
listed_description: Simple encryption library based on Qt for C++ projects.
reason: README only says 'Fast encryption library supporting RSA and AES' and that 'The OpenSSL library is better for security and performance'; no numbers, no named baseline, no benchmark in the repo (tests/ holds CMakeLists.txt, Qt-SecretTest.pro, main.cpp). Repository archived 2025-09-10.

name: retter
listed_description: A collection of hash functions, ciphers, tools, libraries, and materials related to cryptography.
reason: Plain-text README (dated 2011, public domain, Python 2.7 build script) describes a collection of links and algorithm sources; no performance claim, no numbers, no benchmark. README.md does not exist (404); the file is named README.

name: sha1collisiondetection
listed_description: Library and command line tool to detect SHA-1 collision in a file.
reason: Not faster than any baseline. README says only 'very fast and takes less than twice the amount of time as regular SHA-1'. Search snippet of the Git commit that added the DC_SHA1 knob (mirror pages not opened) reports it slower than the incumbents: 1.75x slower than block-sha1 and 2.7x slower than OpenSSL SHA-1 (packfile hash 3.580s sha1dc vs 2.046s block-sha1 vs 1.335s OpenSSL). Source files (sha1.c, ubc_check.c) carry no speed comparisons. Possible reference-list entry as a safety tool with measured overhead, if the orchestrator wants it.

name: Themis
listed_description: crypto library for painless data security, providing symmetric and asymmetric encryption, secure sockets with forward secrecy, for mobile and server platforms.
reason: README has no performance claim. benches/README.md only measures wrapper overhead against Themis Core (self-baseline, no numbers). Themis sits on top of OpenSSL or BoringSSL as the primitive source; a web search found no Themis speed comparison against OpenSSL or libsodium.

name: Tink
listed_description: A multi-language, cross-platform library that provides cryptographic APIs that are secure, easy to use correctly, and hard(er) to misuse.
reason: README has no performance claim or numbers; no benchmark directory in the repo (cc, go, java_src, python, docs, ...); repository archived 2024-04-17 (code split into per-language repos). Web search found no Tink throughput comparison against OpenSSL, BoringSSL or Bouncy Castle. Design goal is misuse resistance, not speed.
